=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/ci_budget_watch.py:105-112 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_job_run_start` falls back to `starts[0]` (the first step in API order) when `min` raises on an unparsable step timestamp, which contradicts the inline comment that says `_seconds` rejects the value.
  WHY: The measured start can be later than the real first step, so the duration is understated and a near-timeout job can be missed or skipped silently. Severity differs between reviewers (NIT from sonnet, minimax and glm, MAJOR from gemini), so the highest is used.
- scripts/ci_budget_watch.py:132 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The job name is interpolated unescaped into the `::notice::` workflow command, without escaping `%`, `\r` or `\n`.
  WHY: A job name with a newline could forge extra workflow commands. Severity differs between reviewers (NIT from sonnet, MAJOR from gemini, hardening-only from minimax), so the highest is used. Sonnet notes that job names come from the repo's own ci.yml.
- scripts/ci_budget_watch.py:83-86 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: `_seconds` catches only `ValueError`, so a naive timestamp mixed with an aware one raises `TypeError`.
  WHY: The `TypeError` would abort `job_duration_findings` for every job, but GitHub always emits `Z` timestamps, so this is not reachable today.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
